title: Across the grid
logline: The first private page. A Sunday grid ruled in blue pencil on the sheet, and the drawing ignoring it: the garage from the doorway, drawn straight across the tiers.

panels.composition: The sheet itself is the subject: faint blue-pencil Sunday tiers ruled and abandoned, and over them, ignoring every line, the garage from its doorway — the long table, the lamp off, the three jars on the sill, the pup asleep in the bed. The drawing crosses the tier lines like they aren't there.

image.prompt: a single full comic page with no panel borders, spare knowing ink line with economy, muted ochre and slate blue and sea-foam green washes, a comic page where faint blue pencil grid lines for a Sunday layout are visible beneath an ink drawing that ignores them completely, a garage studio from its doorway with a long drafting table, a lamp off, three jars on a windowsill and a small three-legged dog asleep in a bed, no words
image.notes: Leave the blue grid faintly visible. The first page of Vol. II; the grid never appears again.

art.line: spare, knowing; economy of line; Era I's black spotting back on purpose in the mill run
art.palette: muted ochres, slate blues, misty sea-foam greens; luminous sunbreaks in the last spring
art.paper: Arches; bristol; the backs of motel registration cards

notes: The grid ruled, then ignored. Day one.
